segments.dry: A reviewer with dry, aging, collagen-depleted skin found it made crepey skin and fine lines less noticeable, though it left a somewhat greasy residue that a moisturizer on top helped remove; another reviewer with dry and aging skin found the formula sticky and wasn't convinced it did more than a toner.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin, including one who applies it near the sensitive eye area, report it doesn't irritate their skin.
segments.mature: Reviewers in their late 40s to 60s report firmer, more lifted, dewier-looking skin with regular use, including reduced crow's feet, smoothed fine lines, and lightened brown marks.

concerns.aging: Many reviewers, especially those using it for anti-aging, report visibly plumper skin, smoothed fine lines around the eyes and mouth, firmer contours, and a more lifted look, in some cases within minutes to a few weeks of regular use; one reviewer, however, didn't notice any lifting effect.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers report the foam absorbs quickly and leaves skin hydrated, soft, and glowing; a couple, though, felt it added little real hydration beyond a light glow, and one noticed unexpected dryness around the forehead after using it multiple times a day for three weeks.
concerns.redness: One reviewer noted the slight redness she normally has around her nose was less noticeable the morning after using the mask.
concerns.spots: One reviewer with dry, collagen-depleted skin reported the brown marks near her eyes visibly lightened alongside smoothed crow's feet.
concerns.blemishes: A couple of reviewers say the mask doesn't cause breakouts and prefer it to silicone-based primers that do; one reviewer, however, reported it broke her out all over her skin.

extraits.titre: So sticky and mixed message instructions
extraits.texte: As a 46 year old with dry and aging skin, I am always trying new products to try and prevent (and potentially undo) wrinkles. I am also a big fan of Korean skincare so I was excited to order Menokin's 30 Seconds Quick Bubble Mask in the Lift Collagen version. I have never tried a bubble mask before so the idea was fascinating. The bottle arrived in a box that was sealed and the bottle itself uses a foaming pump to distribute. The directions are confusing as the box says to pump on your fingertips and massage in (very basic), but the bottle itself has the worlds tiniest print instructions and says to apply 2-3 pumps, 2-3 times. I am not sure which of these instructions are accurate so I tried both ways. Either way, this seems more like a toner than a mask. One pump left my face a bit sticky and never fully absorbed but at the same time, it felt soft and nourished. 3 pumps left my face a bit sticker and ultimately about the same, so I don't see a benefit to using much more than one pump. I do appreciate that the application method here is mess free and easy to use. The ad for this product mentions using more than 2=3 pumps will leave your skin sticky - but again, even one pump did this. Even at one pump per use, I don't see getting 70 sheet masks worth out of it. Scent wise - it has the faintest fruity or floral scent but it's so light and dissipates quickly. As far as ingredients go, I'd say this is just ok. Nothing too exciting but does contain niacinamide, hyaluronic acid an

I've been using this product daily for a couple of weeks, applying one pump to my face. It absorbs quickly—within about 30 seconds of massaging it in—and hasn't caused any irritation. There's no noticeable scent, which I appreciate, and it does provide some hydration. However, it leaves my skin feeling tacky after application, which I don’t love. Because of this, I’ve been hesitant to layer it with other products and have only been using it alongside sunscreen. The label says no rinsing is required, so I assumed it could replace my regular serum—but unfortunately, it doesn't perform as well. I haven’t noticed any significant improvement in my skin, and the sticky residue makes it less pleasant to use. While it might work for others, I don’t see enough benefit to keep it in my routine and will likely discontinue use.

extraits.titre: The easiest moisturizing "mask" I have ever used.
extraits.texte: I don't wear much make-up except for when I go out. I'm usually in and out of my house so to leave this mask on as I go about my day would be a dust/dirt collector. So, I have been using this leave-on mask only at night, overnight as I sleep because they are very sticky. After washing my face after every time I treat my face and neck to this mask, I notice my skin is firmer and not so dragged down. My skin is brighter and the slight redness that I have around my nose is not so obvious the morning after. I am mid-century old and I still get carded so I must be doing something right. I really think this leave-on sticky mask may be contributing to my healthy skin. So yes, I do recommend this product especially if you don't mind the incredibly stickiness. The product is made in Korea.
